claims.text: Anthropic's post on Scion observes that when the clients are agents they are always online, there are many of them, and the expensive thing is moving bytes nobody needs.
claims.quote: when the clients are agents, they are always online, there are many of them, and the expensive thing is moving bytes nobody needs

claims.text: On 16 October the newsroom's vault had 1,295 commits, 5,281 files, 16,315 blobs and 16,391 trees, about 35,000 encrypted objects and 527 MB with all its history.
claims.quote: On 16 October it had 1,295 commits, 5,281 files, 16,315 blobs and 16,391 trees

claims.text: 68 of the vault's commits arrived in the two days before the measurements, which is why it is the best test the team has.
claims.quote: 68 of its commits arrived in the two days before these measurements

claims.text: The vault is in the same range as real application source code: the SG/Send application's git repository has 5,584 files, 4,399 commits and 42,434 objects.
claims.quote: The vault is in the same range as real application source code.

claims.text: The vault lives on the hosted service, S3 behind CloudFront with a small API in front, and the agents reach it through the CLI.
claims.quote: It lives on the hosted service, S3 behind CloudFront with a small API in front

claims.text: A full clone of the vault takes three and a half minutes, and nobody needs one.
claims.quote: Nobody clones all of it. Three and a half minutes, and nobody needs to.

claims.text: One 130-file folder with one commit of history takes 13 seconds and 3 MB, however large the vault is, because the clone asks only for the spine of trees down to its folder and the blobs under it.
claims.quote: A clone that carries a depth costs seconds and megabytes however large the vault is

value.unit: seconds for one folder, one commit

claims.text: A clone that carries the whole history of a folder pays for the history, not the folder: 227 seconds for 130 files, almost all of it walking 1,295 commits one request at a time.
claims.quote: 227 seconds for 130 files, almost all of it walking 1,295 commits one request at a time

value.unit: seconds for one folder with all its history

claims.text: The fix for the history walk is designed: a small encrypted record of the commit chain, written on every push, so a clone can fetch the chain in about 26 batched requests instead of discovering it.
claims.quote: a small encrypted record of the commit chain, written on every push

claims.text: Until 14 October pull was the slow path on this vault, one request per commit and one per blob, and an agent a day behind waited the best part of an hour.
claims.quote: an agent a day behind waited the best part of an hour

claims.text: The CLI team fixed pull on the vault where the agents reported it: blobs now come in batches of 50 with 16 requests in flight, and past a long gap the client lists the store and sweeps what is missing.
claims.quote: blobs now come in batches of 50 with 16 requests in flight

claims.text: After the fix, fetching the whole head into an empty store takes about three minutes, down from about 53; a pull with nothing new takes 2.5 seconds.
claims.quote: takes about three minutes, down from about 53

value.unit: minutes to fetch the whole head into an empty store

claims.text: With the same 35,000 objects on local disk, the one-folder, one-commit clone fell from 13 seconds to 2.3 with a plain file server and 0.8 with the API server as a local process.
claims.quote: The one-folder, one-commit clone fell from 13 seconds to 2.3 and 0.8.

value.unit: seconds for one folder, one commit, from local disk

claims.text: sgit is not the bottleneck; the distance to the storage is, because each request to the hosted service pays a round trip through a CDN, a Lambda and S3 before a byte moves.
claims.quote: So sgit is not the bottleneck; the distance to the storage is.

claims.text: The ruv.sgit hive runs say the same from the other side: on a local server every sgit operation in fifteen recorded runs took between 0.4 and 1.5 seconds, including starting Python and deriving the key.
claims.quote: every sgit operation in fifteen recorded runs took between 0.4 and 1.5 seconds

claims.text: Earlier measurements on a single local server process found ten clones of one folder at once took 1.9 seconds with the server mostly idle, while ten full clones queued to 21 seconds.
claims.quote: ten clones of one folder at once took 1.9 seconds with the server mostly idle

value.unit: seconds for ten simultaneous one-folder clones

claims.text: Vaults of this size are where sgit becomes useful for more than agents' memory, including source code.
claims.quote: I think vaults this size are where sgit becomes useful for more than agents' memory, including source code

claims.text: The next test the owner wants is a real code base moved into a vault, with agents working on it, each cloning the one package it works on in seconds.
claims.quote: a real code base, moved into a vault, with agents working on it

claims.text: Not proven at Scion's scale: 35,000 objects, 1,295 commits and ten agents is the largest vault the team runs, while Scion's monorepo has 100 GB of history and 30,000 merges a day.
claims.quote: Scion's monorepo has 100 GB of history and 30,000 merges a day

claims.text: No blame or bisect: path history, signed commits, signed tags and verification exist; blame is not written yet.
claims.quote: Path history, signed commits, signed tags and verification exist; blame is not written yet.

claims.text: A partial clone of a long history is slow without a depth today; the fix is designed, not shipped.
claims.quote: The fix is designed, not shipped.

claims.text: The measurements are one run each, from sandboxes that send every request through a proxy; a plain connection does better.
claims.quote: One run each, from sandboxes that send every request through a proxy.

claims.text: The source-code use is a proposal: the vault holds notes, mail and analysis, not code.
claims.quote: The vault holds notes, mail and analysis, not code.

claims.text: The vault's measurements are the CLI team's, from 14 and 16 October, with sgit 0.22.0 and the 14 October fixes; the vault's id and contents are not published.
claims.quote: from 14 and 16 October, with sgit 0.22.0 and the 14 October fixes
